title: Full-Bridge Converter (isolated)
summary: Galvanically isolated buck-derived converter; four switches in an H-bridge drive the full input across the transformer primary, and a full-wave secondary rectifier feeds an LC output filter. The CCM ratio is n * D, where n = N2/N1 is the turns ratio. The transformer is driven symmetrically (self-resetting) and there is no right-half-plane zero. Each switch blocks the full bus voltage Vin.

ports.name: in
ports.description: Positive primary-side input bus rail feeding the H-bridge (S1/S3 high side).

ports.name: sw_a
ports.description: First bridge midpoint between S1 (high) and S4 (low); one terminal of the transformer primary.

ports.name: sw_b
ports.description: Second bridge midpoint between S3 (high) and S2 (low); the other terminal of the transformer primary.

ports.name: out
ports.description: Isolated regulated output rail across the LC filter and load (secondary side).

ports.name: pri_gnd
ports.description: Primary-side ground reference (input return); the low-side switches S2/S4 return here.

ports.name: sec_gnd
ports.description: Secondary-side ground reference (output return), galvanically isolated from pri_gnd.

ports.name: pwm
ports.description: Gate-drive commands for the two diagonal switch pairs (S1+S2 and S3+S4), each pair on for duty D within its half-period, with dead-time.

parameters.name: Vin
parameters.description: Primary-side input bus voltage (VB); the full bus is applied across the transformer primary each half-cycle.

parameters.name: fsw
parameters.description: Per-switch-pair switching frequency; the output filter sees ripple at 2*fsw because both half-cycles deliver energy.

parameters.name: D
parameters.description: Steady-state duty cycle of each diagonal switch pair, defined as the on-time within its half switching period.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Power transformer turns ratio n = N2/N1 (secondary over primary).

parameters.name: R_load
parameters.description: Load resistance seen at the output (R_load = Vout / Iout).

parameters.name: r_L
parameters.description: Output inductor series resistance (DCR); dominant loss term affecting the DC conversion ratio.

parameters.name: r_C
parameters.description: Output capacitor equivalent series resistance (ESR); sets the high-frequency zero.

design_equations.name: turns_ratio
design_equations.description: Power transformer turns ratio definition (Alonso eq. 7.3).

design_equations.name: conversion_ratio
design_equations.description: Ideal CCM DC conversion ratio (Alonso eq. 7.5.1 summary lossless); the buck ratio D scaled by the turns ratio n. The H-bridge applies the full bus Vin to the primary, so there is no 1/2 divider factor (twice the half-bridge ratio).

design_equations.name: conversion_ratio_with_losses
design_equations.expression: Vout / Vin = n * D / (1 + r_L / R_load)
design_equations.description: CCM DC conversion ratio including the output inductor series resistance r_L (Alonso eq. 7.5.1 summary); the capacitor ESR does not affect the DC ratio because no DC current flows in C.

design_equations.name: inductor_current
design_equations.description: Average output inductor current equals the load current in CCM (the LC filter keeps the output current continuous, as in a buck).

design_equations.name: inductor_ripple
design_equations.description: Peak-to-peak output inductor current ripple in CCM (Alonso eq. 7.5.1 summary); the buck ripple with the reflected primary voltage n*Vin.

design_equations.name: output_ripple
design_equations.description: Peak-to-peak output voltage ripple in CCM for an ideal capacitor (Alonso eq. 7.5.1 summary); ESR adds r_C * dI_L on top. The 1/16 factor (vs. 1/8 for the buck) is because the output filter is refreshed twice per switching period (effective ripple frequency 2*fsw).

design_equations.name: rectifier_peak_current
design_equations.description: Peak current through each secondary rectifier D1-D4 and the output inductor in CCM (Alonso eq. 7.5.1 summary).

design_equations.name: switch_peak_current
design_equations.description: Peak current through each primary switch S1-S4 in CCM (Alonso eq. 7.5.1 summary); the reflected inductor peak current.

design_equations.name: switch_peak_voltage
design_equations.description: Peak blocking voltage across each primary switch (Alonso eq. 7.5.1 summary); each of the four H-bridge switches blocks only the full bus Vin (plus any leakage spike) - the key advantage over the push-pull, whose switches see 2*Vin. No reset winding is needed - the symmetric bidirectional drive self-resets the core.

design_equations.name: rectifier_peak_voltage
design_equations.description: Peak reverse voltage across each secondary rectifier D1-D4 (Alonso eq. 7.5.1 summary).

design_equations.name: boundary_load_resistance
design_equations.description: CCM-DCM boundary load resistance (Alonso eq. 7.5.1 summary): CCM when R_load < R_lim, DCM when R_load > R_lim. The factor 4 (vs. 2 for the buck/forward) follows from the doubled effective output ripple frequency 2*fsw.

design_equations.name: boundary_output_current
design_equations.description: Output current at the CCM-DCM boundary (Alonso eq. 7.5.1 summary; Io_lim = Vout / R_lim).

design_equations.name: dcm_conversion_ratio
design_equations.expression: Vout / Vin = 2 * n / (1 + sqrt(1 + 4 * k / D**2)),  k = 4 * L * fsw / R_load
design_equations.description: DCM DC conversion ratio (Alonso eq. 7.5.2 summary); load-dependent, with the doubled-frequency factor k = 4*L*fsw/R_load. Twice the half-bridge DCM ratio.

design_equations.name: dcm_peak_inductor_current
design_equations.expression: i_pk = D * (n * Vin - Vout) / (2 * L * fsw)
design_equations.description: Peak inductor (and reflected switch) current in DCM (Alonso eq. 7.5.2 summary).

design_equations.name: ccm_characteristic_polynomial
design_equations.expression: Den(s) = L*C*(1 + r_C/R_load)*s**2 + (L/R_load + r_C*C + r_L*C + r_L*r_C*C/R_load)*s + (1 + r_L/R_load)
design_equations.description: Shared CCM denominator of every small-signal transfer function below; identical to the buck and forward (a complex pole pair near 1/(2*pi*sqrt(L*C))), because the full-bridge is dynamically a buck seen through the transformer.

design_equations.name: control_to_output_tf_ccm
design_equations.description: Control-to-output transfer function in CCM (Alonso eq. 7.5.1 summary); the buck Gd(s) scaled to n*Vin (= (Vout/D)*(1 + r_L/R_load)). Single ESR zero at 1/(r_C*C), no right-half-plane zero. Identical in form to the forward converter.

design_equations.name: audio_susceptibility_tf_ccm
design_equations.description: Input-to-output (audio susceptibility) transfer function in CCM (Alonso eq. 7.5.1 summary); the buck Gb(s) scaled by n, same dynamics as Gd(s).

design_equations.name: output_impedance_tf_ccm
design_equations.description: Open-loop output impedance in CCM (Alonso eq. 7.5.1 summary); identical to the buck/forward and independent of the turns ratio (the secondary side is a plain LC filter). Zo(0) approx r_L, Zo(inf) approx r_C.

design_equations.name: input_impedance_tf_ccm
design_equations.description: Open-loop input impedance in CCM (Alonso eq. 7.5.1 summary); the buck input impedance divided by n**2*D**2, with Zi(0) = (R_load + r_L)/(n**2*D**2). Unlike the half-bridge there is no input-capacitor divider to parallel.

control_notes: The full-bridge converter is dynamically a buck converter seen through the power transformer: four switches in an H-bridge apply the full bus Vin (both polarities) to the primary, and a full-wave secondary rectifier (D1-D4) feeds a continuous-current LC output filter. Its CCM small-signal model is identical in form to the forward converter: the control-to-output plant Gd(s) is a second-order low-pass with a complex LC pole pair and a single ESR zero at 1/(r_C*C), with NO right-half-plane zero. Every CCM transfer function is the buck result scaled through the transformer: Gd = n*Vin*(...)/Den (= (Vout/D)*(1 + r_L/R_load)*...), Gb = n*D*(...)/Den, Zo is identical to the buck (independent of n), and Zi is the buck value divided by n**2*D**2. Compared with the half-bridge, the full-bridge applies twice the primary voltage, so every gain is doubled (ratio n*D vs n*D/2) and there is no input-capacitor divider in Zi. Voltage-mode control with a Type-II/Type-III compensator is straightforward; cross over well below fsw/5 (note the output ripple frequency is 2*fsw), or use current-mode to drop the plant to first order. In DCM (R_load > R_lim = 4*L*fsw/(1-D)) the plant collapses to first order and the DC gain becomes load-dependent. Distinctive full-bridge features: the transformer is driven symmetrically in both directions, so it self-resets (no reset/tertiary winding, no D < 0.5 duty limit); each of the four switches blocks only the full bus Vin (half the push-pull stress); and the boundary and ripple carry a doubled effective frequency (R_lim = 4*L*fsw/(1-D), dVout = dI_L/(16*C*fsw)). Watch for flux-imbalance/DC magnetizing current from asymmetric switch timing (a DC-blocking capacitor or current-mode control mitigates it), add a leakage snubber, and honor the diagonal-pair dead-time to avoid shoot-through. Feedback must cross the isolation barrier (optocoupler + shunt reference, or primary-side regulation). All small-signal results follow from the averaged dependent-source model: the switches are replaced by their average current sources and the rectifier diodes by their average voltage sources, then linearized about the DC operating point.

reference.source: J. Marcos Alonso, Modelling, Control and Simulation of DC-DC Converters
